picks.tribute_angle: oMLX is an LLM inference server with continuous batching and paged SSD KV caching for Apple Silicon, managed from the macOS menu bar. The novel move: a tiered KV cache (hot RAM + cold SSD in safetensors format) where the prefix cache survives server restarts. mlx-lm worked for demos but redid full prefill on every request — oMLX fixes the inference layer that everyone else skipped. Drop-in OpenAI and Anthropic API compatible at localhost:8000. Jun Kim, data engineer by day, AI dreamer by night, building from Seoul since the MLX ecosystem needed it.
voice_notes: Build-in-public engineer, doesn't oversell — lets the cache stats speak
The hook is the persistence model: KV cache survives restarts
Frame as the inference layer Apple Silicon was missing, not another inference server
prior_work: mlx-lm ecosystem contributions (indirect — oMLX built atop mlx-lm BatchGenerator)

picks.headline_metric: 795 stars | 444 HN points (top AI/ML story) | 26M parameters
picks.tribute_angle: Needle is a 26M-parameter Simple Attention Network distilled from Gemini 3.1, designed to run on watches, phones, and glasses, and scoped exclusively to single-shot function calling. The architecture strips out all feedforward layers — only attention — because attention compiles to GEMMs that mobile NPUs already handle. The win is not conversation; the README says so. The win is function call accuracy at a size no one else is targeting. Henry Ndubuaku, 4x ICLR author, YC S25, built Cactus (4.8k stars on-device inference engine) first. Needle is the research artifact that justifies the product.
voice_notes: Plainspoken about scale — names competitors and their trade-offs directly
Architectural honesty: Simple Attention Network is literally no feedforward, only attention
MANIFESTO framework: the project itself is a position, a stake in the ground
prior_work: Cactus — low-latency mobile inference engine (4.8k stars)
